# Solution design assessment

## Evidence and scope

- Pinned story: `user_story`, `characters 0-16000` -- Python 3.12, Flask, server-rendered password-reset pages, pytest, synthetic accounts, in-memory notifications, documented production limitations; no deployment or deployment workflows.
- Supplied image: attachment `457acc5e-8bce-44d6-abec-d204c28e4d84`, `sign-in-wireframe.png`. I observed a centered bordered sign-in panel on white, bold "Sign in" heading, labeled email and password fields (placeholders `name@example.com` and masked `********`), blue underlined "Forgot password?" link below the password field, wide dark "Sign in" button, and muted "No account? Contact your administrator." footer. This is sign-in visual evidence only, not proof of navigation, authentication, precise CSS values, or recovery-page layout.
- Curated account recovery standard: knowledge `28e06fb4-ccd1-4117-8f7b-b2a6c9bfaf1f`, `v1, chunk 0` (ACC-STD-01 through ACC-STD-03). It requires identical request responses regardless of account existence, five reset requests per account per hour, single-use links expiring 30 minutes after issuance, sign-out of every active session after a successful reset, and an owner notification after every successful reset. A separate search for additional organization architecture/technology standards returned none; do not cite or assume any.
- Approved predecessor `requirements_analysis`: REQ-001 through REQ-018 with acceptance criteria. Approved `ui_analysis`: observed sign-in hierarchy plus explicitly *proposed* recovery states and accessibility behavior, not additional mandated UI specifications. Approved `acceptance_20261028191242_8eaf7f_risk`: RD8CDC-001 through RD8CDC-006 are prospective verification risks, not observed defects or test results. Each prior output was read using its approved stage key. Repository README describes a disposable SDLC repository; no application implementation is present to evaluate.

## Design implications for planning

- Cover REQ-001/002/013/014 with Flask-rendered sign-in and recovery entry; REQ-003/004/005 with account-independent public request responses, per-account rolling-hour cap, and internal issuance; REQ-006/007/008 with guarded one-time token consumption, issue-time expiry boundary, and password change; REQ-009/010 with all-session invalidation and owner notification after each success; REQ-011/012 with synthetic account state and an in-memory sink; REQ-015/016 with pytest and production-limitations documentation. REQ-017/018 require explicit no-deploy/no-workflow acceptance checks in a delivery task rather than deployment work. Every requirement must link to an implementation or verification task, or receive a justified coverage disposition.
- Identify component and data contracts for Flask routes/templates, synthetic account/session/token/request state, recovery service, notification sink, and controlled clock; test equal visible responses, rate-limit rollover, expiration exactly at 30 minutes, replay, session invalidation, and notifications. Keep tokens and account inventory out of public responses. Volatile storage is an intentional exercise limitation, not production-safe persistence or notification delivery. No deployment target, infrastructure, or workflow is authorized.
- Material decisions to document at design time include token generation/storage, per-account rolling-window accounting, password hashing, session invalidation mechanism, atomicity/replay handling, and testable time. Compare alternatives rather than presenting the exercise architecture as production hardened.

## Unknowns and evidence limits

- Sign-in success semantics and the existence/implementation of active sessions are not specified. Design must make REQ-009 verifiable when sessions exist without falsely claiming that the wireframe defines a sign-in destination or authentication contract.
- No mandated recovery-page copy/layout or new-password policy is supplied; distinguish proposed accessible UI behavior from approved requirements. No implemented service, running tests, live notification integration, production datastore, or deployment evidence was provided.
- The image-reading tool supplied a reference only; the visual observations above come from the image attached to this conversation and align with the approved UI analysis. Stage-output tool responses did not supply independent `stage_output` reference locators: preserve their approved IDs and original evidence references, and do not fabricate locators.

Assessment only. Planning and product outputs await the next approved phase.
